name: mcs-03-single-cell-heterogeneity
title: Arc 3 — single-cell heterogeneity from molecular noise

cites.claim: interdivision-time CV ~10-30% and the adder principle in E. coli

question: Across a seed ensemble, does v2ecoli produce lawful single-cell heterogeneity — an interdivision-time coefficient of variation in the ~10-30% E. coli range and adder-like size homeostasis (constant added size, slope ~0 of added vs birth size)? Where the model's heterogeneity is unlawful (too deterministic, or non-adder), what small correction to the stochastic sources restores it?
hypothesis: Stochastic gene expression and stochastic replication initiation make the seeds diverge, yielding division_time CV ~10-30% and an adder slope near 0. If the ensemble is too tight (CV too low) or homeostasis is not adder-like, the dominant missing noise source is identifiable and correctable.
objective: Run an ecoli_baseline seed ensemble and measure the division_time distribution, its CV, and the added-size vs birth-size relationship to characterize how molecular noise becomes population-level heterogeneity.

baseline.detail: Seed ensemble (>=8 seeds) on basal medium, multi-generation.

variants.name: seed-ensemble
variants.detail: Multi-seed ensemble (measures the native heterogeneity distribution; no model perturbation). The stochastic-timing perturbation is the mcs-06 variant.

model_settings.name: seed-ensemble
model_settings.detail: Vary seed across the ensemble; each seed is an independent stochastic lineage.

expected_behavior.name: division-time-cv-in-band
expected_behavior.rationale: Interdivision-time CV in E. coli is ~10-30%; a value far below indicates the model is too deterministic, far above indicates runaway noise.

expected_behavior.name: size-homeostasis-adder
expected_behavior.rationale: Adder principle: added size is independent of birth size (slope ~0).

measure.detail: CV = sd(division_time)/mean(division_time) over post-burn-in cells across the ensemble; band 0.10-0.30.

tests.name: size-homeostasis-adder
tests.question: Is size homeostasis adder-like (added vs birth size slope ~0)?

measure.detail: Linear regression of (division_mass - birth_mass) on birth_mass; slope near 0 = adder.

readouts: division_time (interdivision time, min) per cell across the seed ensemble; CV

visualizations.name: Heterogeneity vs biological band
visualizations.description: Interdivision-time distribution: model CV ~7% against the shaded 10-30% biological band; adder plot.

division-time-cv-in-band.detail: Interdivision-time CV 0.070 (mean tau 49.3 min) — below the biological 0.10-0.30 band. CV accumulates across generations: 0.000 (gen2, identical across seeds) -> 0.029 (gen3) -> 0.050 (gen4). The model under-produces cell-to-cell heterogeneity.

size-homeostasis-adder.detail: Added-vs-birth slope 0.59, but birth mass spans only 309-358 fg (CV ~4%), so the adder/sizer/timer distinction is not resolvable — the low birth-size variation is itself a consequence of the under-dispersion.

claim: v2ecoli under-produces single-cell heterogeneity: interdivision-time CV is ~7% (mean tau 49 min) against a biological 10-30%, accumulating slowly across generations (0%->5% over gens 2-4). The cells stay more synchronized than real E. coli, and birth-size variation is too small to classify size homeostasis. The gap is structural (the model runs many processes at expected rather than fully stochastic rates), not a small parameter — a landed correction would require enabling additional stochastic mechanisms. [Follow-ups: mcs-10 confirms the under-dispersion is robust across 6 seeds (pooled CV 0.048) and resolves adder-like homeostasis (slope ~0); mcs-06 then LANDS a fix — a stochastic D-period lifts the CV to 0.115, into the biological 0.10-0.30 band, with the mean generation time approximately preserved.]

findings.statement: Across a 6-seed ensemble, v2ecoli's interdivision-time coefficient of variation is 7% (mean generation time 49 min), well below the 10-30% measured in single-cell E. coli. The heterogeneity is real but slow to develop: sibling lineages started from different seeds are IDENTICAL in division time at generation 2 (CV 0.000), diverging only to 3% by generation 3 and 5% by generation 4. Birth mass spans just 309-358 fg (CV ~4%), too narrow to resolve whether the cell is an adder, sizer or timer — and that narrowness is itself the signature of under-dispersion. The whole-cell model is more deterministic / synchronized than real cells, consistent with its use of expected (mean) rates in many processes rather than fully stochastic kinetics. Closing this gap is a structural modeling change (adding stochastic mechanisms), not a parameter tweak, so it is flagged rather than applied here.

expected.summary: Single-cell E. coli shows interdivision-time CV ~10-30% and clear adder-like size homeostasis.

findings.next_action: Localize the missing noise: audit which processes run at expected rather than stochastic rates (division D-period, replication initiation timing, low-copy expression) and whether an existing stochastic mode can be enabled. Structural change; out of scope for a small fix.
caveats: Small ensemble (6 seeds, 3 post-burn-in gens); the CV estimate has wide uncertainty but is robustly below the biological band across every generation.

biological_summary: Stochastic gene expression and replication initiation should make no two cells identical, giving an interdivision-time CV of ~10–30% and adder-like size homeostasis. v2ecoli under-produces this: it is more synchronized/deterministic than real E. coli.

behavior_tests.name: division-time-cv-in-band
behavior_tests.measure: CV of interdivision time across a 6-seed ensemble

behavior_tests.name: size-homeostasis-adder
behavior_tests.observed: 0.59, but birth-size CV ~4% too narrow to resolve

conclusion: ## Result The model is under-dispersed (CV 7% vs 10–30%). A code audit (see mcs-06) traces it to a bypassed division-noise term; the fix is a structural modeling change, flagged not applied.
